title: pvWriteDataSetCSVWriter
body:
## pvWriteDataSetCSVWriter

Legacy alias of pvWriteCSVWriter: ParaView keeps DataSetCSVWriter, a proxy derived from CSVWriter with the same class and settings, only for old state files and traces. It writes the same delimited text (one row per point, cell or table row, one column per component) and is verified the same way under the table contract. Prefer pvWriteCSVWriter in new documents.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Precision defaults to 5 significant digits; raise it (17 reproduces doubles exactly) or set an export tolerance, otherwise verification usually fails.
- Verification covers one dataset or table: composite input is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_DATA_TYPE (merge it with pvMergeBlocks first). The verifier uses the FieldAssociation, FieldDelimiter, StringDelimiter and UseStringDelimiter that ParaView holds on the created writer, so a .tsv file is checked with the tab ParaView sets for it. Author FieldAssociation as ParaView's entry text, for example "Cell Data". When it is omitted, ParaView picks (and Schemaxis reads back) the first of Point, Cell, Vertex, Edge, Row then Field Data that has arrays and tuples, which is not always the points. Only "Point Data", "Cell Data" and (for tables) "Row Data" can be verified: "Field Data", "Vertex Data" or "Edge Data" is rejected at planning with UNSUPPORTED_ASSOCIATION, and "Row Data" for a non-table input fails verification with the same fault; a delimiter longer than one character gives UNSUPPORTED_DELIMITER.
- ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE) because the table comparison needs every input array in the file; filter arrays with pvPassArrays and export that node.
- An earlier catalogue run (verification/2026-09-16-catalogue-expansion.json, writerQualification) passed only on a small serial fixture with Precision 17 and the other options at their defaults; no current native acceptance check is recorded, so verify the export on representative data.

Native constructor: `DataSetCSVWriter`. Identity: `writers/DataSetCSVWriter`. Role: `writer`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Connect upstream object to `Input` | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkCompositeDataSet","vtkDataSet","vtkTable"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AddMetaData` | It is possible for this filter to add additional meta-data to the field data such as point coordinates (when point attributes are selected and input is point-set) or structured coordinates etc. To enable this addition of extra information, turn this flag on. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `AddTime` | When set, the writer will add a "Time" column to the generated file indicating the current dataset time, if any. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `AddTimeStep` | When set, the writer will add a "TimeStep" column to the generated file indicating the current dataset time step, if any. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `CellDataArrays` | Select the cell data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ChooseArraysToWrite` | Explicitly choose which arrays to write. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `EdgeDataArrays` | Select the edge data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FieldAssociation` | Attribute data that the writer turns into rows: one row per point, cell, vertex, edge or table row, or the field-data tuples. Chosen by the ParaView entry text: "Point Data", "Cell Data", "Vertex Data", "Edge Data", "Row Data" or "Field Data". ParaView offers only the associations the connected input has (for example "Row Data" for a table), so a text it does not offer fails with NATIVE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH when the node is configured. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Point Data","Cell Data","Vertex Data","Edge Data","Row Data","Field Data"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Point Data"` |
| `FieldDataArrays` | Select the field data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FieldDelimiter` | Used to set the delimiter character. This is hidden from the user and set automatically based on the file extension. An extension of .tsv will set the delimiter character to a tab. Otherwise a comma will be used as the delimiter. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `PointDataArrays` | Select the point data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Precision` | Number of digits vtkCSVWriter prints for floating-point values. With UseScientificNotation false (ParaView's default) it counts significant digits, so the default 5 writes 101325.7 as 1.0133e+05; with UseScientificNotation true it counts digits after the decimal point of the mantissa. Integer columns are not affected. | `{"minimum":0,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0` |
| `RowDataArrays` | Select the row data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `StringDelimiter` | Used to set the delimiter used for string data, if any, eg. double quotes("). | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `UseScientificNotation` | When true, every floating-point value is written in scientific notation (101325.7 with Precision 5 becomes 1.01326e+05) and Precision counts decimals of the mantissa. When false, the general format switches between fixed and exponent notation and Precision counts significant digits. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseStringDelimiter` | Used to enable StringDelimiter for string data. Enabled by default. Turn this off if you do not want quotes around the column headers. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `VertexDataArrays` | Select the vertex data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Output publication contract:

```json
{
  "comparison": "table",
  "extensions": [
    "csv",
    "txt",
    "tsv"
  ],
  "filenames": "managed output directory",
  "losses": [
    "topology",
    "coordinates",
    "structure"
  ],
  "qualification": "requires fixture",
  "time": "one scheduled state"
}
```

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "explicit exports with semantic readback",
  "outputPorts": 0,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `scenes[].exports`; writers cannot be graph nodes. The main data input is `node`; non-data ports go in `resources`.

```json
{
  "id": "exportResult",
  "node": "DATA_NODE",
  "writer": "pvWriteDataSetCSVWriter",
  "acceptLosses": [
    "topology",
    "coordinates",
    "structure"
  ]
}
```
